id: We are not one people: From Parihaka to a Pākehā myth-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
name: We are not one people: From Parihaka to a Pākehā myth
venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
long_description:
On the morning of the 5th November 1881, an Irishman called Andrew Gilhooly formed up alongside other members of the Armed Constabulary at the entrance to Parihaka pā; he was there for the invasion, the occupation and — much later — for the farming of land taken from Taranaki iwi.

But those events dropped out of the family stories handed down to Gilhooly’s descendants; neither do they feature in national narratives of fairness, egalitarianism and equal treatment.

In this presentation, Richard Shaw, one of Gilhooly’s descendants, will explore the relationship between historical amnesia amongst (some) descendants of settler families and the stories we tell each other of the nation we live in.

venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The block starts Mon 24 August and runs for 8 weeks till Mon 12 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

This class is a mixed-level class, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

long_description:
Bring along a painting and a suitable frame, either a cheapo from Briscoes or a good second hand frame. We will provide all the tools, process and materials to frame your piece of art.
It’s a practical course where you will learn to prepare the frame, cut with a knife, measure and cut a matt with the matt cutter.

You will walk away with your painting framed, ready to hang and some useful knowledge about framing ready for sale, exhibition standards, D rings, swing tags, acid free archival materials, tape, and how to hang a painting on the wall.

What’s included in this workshop:

- Demonstration steps to framing your work
- Assembling the tools you need
- Choosing and cleaning frames
- How to size and cut an acid free mat
- What sort of tapes to use for each task
- Various fixings for hanging and D-rings
- Replacing acid leaching materials with foam board
- Cutting techniques

long_description:
This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 25 August and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 13 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
long_description:
A chance meeting in Italy in 2021 sparked a partnership between Hungarian cellist Balázs Dolfin and Chinese-New Zealand pianist Tony Chen Lin. Trained in Hungary and Germany, they bring dynamic energy and deep rapport, drawing on global influences while still calling Budapest their enduring musical home. Tony has played solo piano for Sunday Concerts.

Their recital opens with Anton Webern’s evocative Sonata for Cello and Piano, followed by J.S. Bach’s Sonata for Viola da Gamba and Harpsichord, a lively, expressive dialogue. Zoltán Kodály’s Sonata, Op. 4 follows, inspired by Hungarian folk music, answered by Gao Ping’s Sonata No. 2 “Departure”, a Chinese counterpart. Belá Bartók’s Rhapsody No. 1 transforms peasant music into vivid concert form. Nathanael Dejong’s Abandoned Voices reflects on disconnection in the digital age. The concert closes with Johannes Brahms’s Sonata in E minor, a work steeped in contrapuntal textures and homage to Bach, bridging Hungary and the deep roots of the cello-piano repertoire.

long_description:
This event will take place in Bleachers, Ground Floor of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library.

The theme of our August musical book club is outsider.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and talk. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil’s bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.


The theme of our August musical book club is outsider.

Music to be performed:
John Dowland | Flow My Tears
Fanny Mendelssohn | String Quartet in Eb Major
Erwin Schulhof | Five pieces for String Quartet
Florence Price | Five Folksongs in Counterpoint

History is littered with artists who stood apart from society, and this month’s musical book club explores some of these outsiders. From Dowland’s melancholic reflection as a religious minority, to Fanny Mendelssohn’s struggle as a woman composing and performing in a male-dominated time, Schulhoff’s political persecution and eventual death in the Wülzburg concentration camp, and Price’s struggle as a Black woman in early 20th-century America.

id: Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs-St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu-Event Finder
name: Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs
venue: St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu
long_description:
“Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.”
These familiar lines from Robert Frost's poem The Road Not Taken form part of Frostiana, Randall Thompson's celebrated setting of Frost's poetry and the centrepiece of Kāpiti Chorale's Session Two programme.
As 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, the choir will explore a selection of American high choral music spanning more than two centuries, from Billings in the eighteenth century to works by 20th and 21st century master composers Thompson, Barber, Bernstein, Copland, Hagenberg, Higdon, Lauridsen, Stroope, Weill, and Whitacre.
The programme brings together music inspired by poetry, folk frontier traditions, sacred texts, and the natural world. Audiences will hear familiar favourites such as Simple Gifts alongside works including Sure On This Shining Night, Dirait-On, The Seal Lullaby, Lux Aurumque, and A Quiet Moment.
Moving between accompanied and a cappella works, the programme offers a wide range of musical styles and moods while showcasing some of the most loved art music in the American choral repertoire.
Kāpiti Chorale will be joined by accompanist Phillip O'Malley and tenor soloist Jamie Young.

long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 27 August and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 15 October, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

name: Sea Shanty Society EP Release Tour
venue: Raumati South Memorial Hall, 16 Tennis Court Rd, Raumati
long_description:
The scuttlebutt is true...

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor-squall of pure shanty.

Singalong shanties! Nautical games! Best dressed prizes!

Limited tickets.

Live review from Maryanne Cathro:

"Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand, he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong, and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

It’s hard to describe the impact of stadium concert-level audience euphoria in a small community hall, yet that is what it is. Bopping bodies, bathed in coloured light, so into the music, which is just fantastic in every way. The dance area is more like an ecstatic mosh pit.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing, and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd."

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

id: Harvest Moon: Highways, Heartaches and Harmonies-Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Harvest Moon: Highways, Heartaches and Harmonies
venue: Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton
long_description:
Wellington Americana band Harvest Moon returns to the Wairarapa Events Centre in August, renewing a relationship with one of New Zealand’s most enthusiastic country music audiences.

The six-piece band has performed in the region on three previous occasions and says Wairarapa audiences have always responded with warmth, enthusiasm and a genuine appreciation for live country and Americana music.

“There has always been a strong country music culture in the Wairarapa,” says band member Wayne Mills. “Every time we’ve played here we’ve been made to feel very welcome, and we’re looking forward to returning.”

Harvest Moon combines guitars, pedal steel, accordion, banjo, dobro and piano with rich vocal harmonies to create an authentic Americana sound inspired by artists including Johnny Cash, Vince Gill, Brad Paisley, Rodney Crowell and The Mavericks.

Fresh from a sell-out show in New Plymouth’s 4th Wall Theatre, and successful recent performances in Whanganui and Feilding, Harvest Moon continues to attract audiences who appreciate outstanding musicianship, memorable songs and an evening of relaxed entertainment.

“Our shows are about more than just the music,” says Mills. “They’re about sharing great songs, having a few laughs and giving people a couple of hours where they can simply enjoy themselves. We know that’s something Wairarapa audiences have always appreciated.”

AI tools like ChatGPT are everywhere, but how do you get the best out of them? In this hands-on, phone-based workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make ChatGPT a more useful, reliable partner in your work and life.
